name: Post Purchase Upsell Hero
summary: One-click post-purchase upsell and downsell offers for Shopify, with targeting rules, AI product recommendations, A/B testing and a revenue dashboard.
best_for: shopify stores that want post purchase upsells for a $19 monthly fee plus a commission capped at $500, and that are comfortable being early on an app a few months old
skip_if: you already do more than $20,000 of upsell revenue a month and would rather pay a flat fee than 2.5% of the first slice, you sell thin-margin add-ons where a revenue percentage eats the profit on the extra sale, or you want an app with more than a few months of track record
honest_knock: The 2.5% comes off revenue, not margin. On a $40 upsell carrying a 20% margin the app takes a dollar of the eight you actually made: fine. On discounted or thin-margin add-ons the same percentage is a far bigger share of the profit, and the meter reads revenue either way. The $19 monthly fee comes on top, and there is no flat option to escape to: a store doing $20,000 of upsell revenue a month pays the full $500 plus the $19 and cannot buy out of the percentage, while the free-above-$20,001 tier only rewards stores already past that line. And the app is young: it launched on 19 June 2026, so at the end of August there were barely ten weeks of merchant experience behind it. Post-purchase offers also depend on your store's checkout supporting the post-purchase extension; check that before you plan around them.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pay on Extra Sales · per month, plus 2.5% of the first $20,000 of monthly upsell revenue
pricing.notes: (Shopify listing, read 16 Nov 2026, USD; our reads of 31 August and 19 September 2026 showed $0 a month, so the monthly fee differs from those reads) One plan, Pay on Extra Sales, at $19 a month plus usage charges, with a 14 day free trial. The usage table, read from the listing's own pricing-estimator data, has two tiers: 2.5% on the first $20,000 of upsell revenue in a month, and $0 from $20,001 up. In practice that is a flat fee plus a commission with a ceiling: usage charges are capped at $500 per cycle, so the most a cycle can cost is $519, and a cycle in which the app sells nothing costs the $19. In the app on 16 Nov 2026 the plan screen showed one plan, Pay on Extra Sales, with $19 struck through and $0 on a development store with 14 trial days, plus the note that regular pricing applies when the store goes live. There is no paid tier above it: unlimited funnels and offers, one-click upsell and downsell, AI product recommendations, analytics and A/B testing and market translations all sit on that single plan. Charges are billed in USD every 30 days. As of 19 Sep 2026 the vendor's own site published no prices at all — its pricing link leads to the same single-plan listing — so the listing is the only place the meter is stated. Neither page defined how 'upsell revenue' is measured, so we asked, and the vendor answered in writing on 21 September 2026 with permission to quote it. The figure is net: the amount the customer is actually charged for the accepted upsell item, after any discount set on that offer, and nothing from the original cart is included. Refunds and cancellations of an accepted upsell are reversed automatically through Shopify — proportionally for partial refunds, with the 2.5% coming off alongside, and no support ticket needed — while refunds of original cart items never move the figure, because they were never billed. There is no multi-day attribution window either: the offer exists only on the Shopify post-purchase page between payment and the order confirmation, and the merchant sets how long that moment stays open, with a default of 20 minutes, any value from 1 to 59 minutes, or Shopify's own 60-minute default. The vendor says the full rule now sits in its help center under Pricing and billing. That is the vendor's account of its own meter, dated and on the record, but it is not something we have audited against a live bill.

compare_with.name: AfterSell
compare_with.why: AfterSell is the established name for post-purchase upsells on Shopify and sells on breadth and track record. Post Purchase Upsell Hero sells on the pricing model: a $19 monthly fee plus 2.5% of the first $20,000 of upsell revenue it generates, nothing above that. If you want the more proven option, that is AfterSell. If you would rather start with a 14 day free trial and a commission that stops at $500, and can live with an app that launched in June 2026, this is the lighter experiment, and the one you can stop before the first charge.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Post Purchase Upsell Hero on the test plan of a Shopify development store: a funnel from a template, publishing it, a test checkout with the test gateway, the offer and downsell after payment, and the uninstall dialog. No offer was accepted and nothing was paid or uninstalled. The checkout setting Use an app to add features at checkout after payment, in Shopify Settings, Checkout, was changed from None to Post Purchase Upsell Hero and saved; the setup guide then showed 1/2. In the app the template More of the same (Ideal for cosmetics, consumables and fashion) was used. A screen Building More of the same went through 4 steps (Reading your catalogue and store category, Picking products that pair well with your bestsellers, Creating the upsell and downsell steps, Applying recommended discounts) and in about 10 seconds gave a funnel Saved as Draft. Upsell 1 offered the most expensive product in the cart; we changed it to Choose manually with the product Selling Plans Ski Wax at $24.95; the discount was 25%. The funnel also has an Upsell 2 (AI Recommendation, 25%) after Accepted and a Downsell 1 (AI Recommendation, 30%) after Declined. Save, then Save changes? and Publish changes gave Changes successfully published and the status Active. A test order through Preview store (no store password was entered; Buy it now in the theme editor opens the Checkout Editor with sample data, so that route failed): a snowboard at $749.95, a made up name, address and email, and the test gateway with card number 1; the checkout itself says 1 simulates an approved transaction. No real payment details were used. After Pay now the post-purchase page showed Special offer today only, Add Selling Plans Ski Wax to your order and save 25%, $24.95 now $18.71, Pay now and Decline offer. Decline led to a downsell for The Complete Snowboard at $699.95 now $489.97 (Save 30%) and a second offer for The Collection Snowboard: Hydrogen at $600.00 now $420.00; both were declined and the thank you page showed only the original product. Nothing was accepted. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 14:53:10 and the offer in view at 14:59:34, so 6 minutes 24 seconds with about 14 main actions, including one failed route through the theme editor and one detour through Preview store. Post-purchase works through the checkout extension of Shopify; no gateway or Plus requirement was seen and the test gateway worked. Offers for PayPal orders need a separate step, requesting reference transactions at PayPal, which was not done. The Settings, Apps row for the app carries the label Free trial; its Uninstall dialog (reason list, feedback box) was opened and cancelled. Not tested: offers by customer type, accepting an offer, A/B tests, analytics with real numbers (the dashboard still showed dashes), the PayPal step, the live price and a move to or comparison with AfterSell. The funnel stays Active and a test order exists in the store. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Buy it now in the theme editor opens the Checkout Editor with sample data and gives no real order, so the test needed Preview store and a cart that first had to be emptied.

The funnel also has an Upsell 2 (AI Recommendation, 25%) after Accepted and a Downsell 1 (AI Recommendation, 30%) after Declined. Save, then Save changes? and Publish changes gave Changes successfully published and the status Active. A test order through Preview store (no store password was entered; Buy it now in the theme editor opens the Checkout Editor with sample data, so that route failed): a snowboard at $749.95, a made up name, address and email, and the test gateway with card number 1; the checkout itself says 1 simulates an approved transaction. No real payment details were used. After Pay now the post-purchase page showed Special offer today only, Add Selling Plans Ski Wax to your order and save 25%, $24.95 now $18.71, Pay now and Decline offer. Decline led to a downsell for The Complete Snowboard at $699.95 now $489.97 (Save 30%) and a second offer for The Collection Snowboard: Hydrogen at $600.00 now $420.00; both were declined and the thank you page showed only the original product. Nothing was accepted. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 14:53:10 and the offer in view at 14:59:34, so 6 minutes 24 seconds with about 14 main actions, including one failed route through the theme editor and one detour through Preview store. Post-purchase works through the checkout extension of Shopify; no gateway or Plus requirement was seen and the test gateway worked. Offers for PayPal orders need a separate step, requesting reference transactions at PayPal, which was not done. The Settings, Apps row for the app carries the label Free trial; its Uninstall dialog (reason list, feedback box) was opened and cancelled. Not tested: offers by customer type, accepting an offer, A/B tests, analytics with real numbers (the dashboard still showed dashes), the PayPal step, the live price and a move to or comparison with AfterSell. The funnel stays Active and a test order exists in the store. No kit records were entered.
